Capital Improvements
Extensive improvements are proposed for this area, as detailed in the Project Description. The geologic hazards to street improvements in the proposed areas are primarily related to the nature of the soils. Weak soils can lead to differential settlement which could crack pavements and curbs, and interfere with drainage of streets, gutters, and sewers.
Expansivity can cause damage to pavements and disrupt curbs and gutters. Corrosivity is a hazard to buried pipelines which experience rapid deterioration. These factors as well as the original standard of construction may well be the basic cause for the deteriorated condition of the streets in the target areas. Evaluation by the City Public Works Department of these factors and the original construction in order to determine the degree of reconstruction required should effectively mitigate these hazards.
The soil properties for strength and expansivity are given for the neighborhoods in the preceding section. Areas of high expansivity are also the areas which have high corrosivity, and areas of moderate expansivity have low corrosivity. Mitigation of these hazards can be implemented by the use of imported non-expansive sub-base material beneath pavements, and the use of coated pipes or non-corroding materials such as plastic, ceramic or concrete.
Seismic phenomena can be a hazard to street improvements. Surface rupture is not a serious hazard to pavements, but buried utilities and sewers would be interrupted. The greatest seismic hazard to streets and related improvements is the potential in some areas for ground failure. Vertical or lateral movement would destroy pavements, interrupt utilities, and interfere with drainage. Areas subject to these hazards are presented in the previous section.
The repair and rebuilding of streets will result in no direct impact with respect to geology; however, after rebuilding, the streets are subject to geologic hazards described above unless proper design considerations are used to mitigate these hazards.
Community Facilities
The outdoor improvements proposed for the Woodrow Wilson playground will have no geologic impact.
Mayfair CNRA:
Housing Rehabilitation/Code Enforcement
The continued program of structural survey and code enforcement will have a positive impact. The identification of structures not in conformace with applicable codes is the first step toward eliminating seismic impacts. Vigorous enforcement of proper codes will likewise have a positive impact. Rehabilitation of substandard housing units will have a positive impact.
